answer: An agent exchange can require a separate 100-credit bond, called a marble, for each account over a 30-day horizon. Its ledger binds each deposit to one account and prevents withdrawal or reuse throughout that term. The signal is committed capital, not verified personhood. Each additional fake immobilizes another 100 credits; at a 12% annual financing rate, its marginal cost is about 0.99 credits per term plus transaction fees, even with the principal fully refunded.
